Volume 1
This entry indicates the first volume of a comprehensive history textbook, covering significant events and themes up to the year 1500.

1500
The year 1500 marks a significant period in world history, representing the close of the Middle Ages and the onset of the Renaissance and Age of Exploration.

World History, Volume 1: to 1500
A comprehensive academic text providing an analysis of world history up to the year 1500, contributing to educational resources in historical studies.

Ann Kordas
Ann Kordas is a senior contributing author associated with Johnson & Wales University, known for her contributions to the field of history.

Ryan J. Lynch
Ryan J. Lynch is a senior contributing author from Columbus State University, contributing significant insights into historical narratives.

Brooke Nelson
Brooke Nelson, formerly associated with California State University, is a senior contributing author, bringing expertise to historical scholarship.

Julie Tatlock
Julie Tatlock from Mount Mary University is recognized as a senior contributing author, enhancing the discourse in world history studies.

OpenStax
OpenStax is a nonprofit ed tech initiative that provides free, peer-reviewed, openly licensed textbooks for college courses and personalized courseware aimed at improving students' educational access and learning.<SEP>OpenStax is a nonprofit organization that provides free and flexible educational resources and textbooks for students and educators.<SEP>OpenStax is an educational organization based at Rice University that provides free, openly licensed textbooks and learning resources.

Rice University
Rice University is a leading research university known for its commitment to undergraduate education, path-breaking research, and diverse community fostering learning and discovery.<SEP>Rice University is a private research university located in Houston, Texas, and it is the institution supporting OpenStax.

Houston, Texas
Houston is a major city in Texas, known for its diverse population and as the home of Rice University.

Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License
This license allows users to share and adapt the textbook content while providing appropriate credit to the original source.

2023
The year 2023 marks the publication date of the textbook content produced by OpenStax.

ISBN-13
ISBN numbers provide unique identifiers for the various print and digital versions of the textbook, crucial for bibliographic references.

Arnold Ventures
Arnold Ventures is a philanthropic organization that supports initiatives aimed at improving educational access and success.

Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is a philanthropic effort that seeks to promote educational access and reform through various partnerships and funding.

Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation is a major philanthropic organization focused on enhancing global health and education.

Google Inc.
Google Inc. is a technology company known for its search engine and various initiatives to enhance educational resources.

National Science Foundation
The National Science Foundation is a government agency that supports fundamental research and education in all fields of science and engineering.

Philanthropic Support
The section discussing Philanthropic Support highlights the various partners contributing to OpenStax's mission of improving educational access.

World History Volume 1
World History Volume 1 is one of the educational resources offered by OpenStax, emphasizing free and accessible learning materials.

Early Human Societies
Unit 1 focuses on early human societies, including the development of a global perspective and key themes related to early civilizations and urban societies.

Understanding the Past
Chapter 1 discusses methods for understanding history, including causation, interpretation, and the significance of primary sources.

Early Humans
Chapter 2 covers early human evolution, migration patterns, and life during the Paleolithic Age and the Neolithic Revolution.

Early Civilizations and Urban Societies
Chapter 3 emphasizes the rise of early civilizations, including significant cultures such as Ancient Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt.

The Near East
Chapter 4 explores historical developments from Old Babylon to the Medes, including the New Kingdom of Egypt and the Persian Empire.

Paleolithic Age
The Paleolithic Age refers to the early period of human history characterized by the use of stone tools and a hunter-gatherer lifestyle.

Neolithic Revolution
The Neolithic Revolution signifies a major turning point in human history marked by the transition from nomadic lifestyles to agriculture and settlement.

Ancient Mesopotamia
Ancient Mesopotamia is known as one of the world's earliest civilizations, emerging around the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, famous for its innovations in writing, agriculture, and urbanization.

Ancient Egypt
Ancient Egypt was a civilization that flourished along the Nile River, renowned for its monumental architecture, hieroglyphics, and complex society centered on agriculture and trade.

Asia in Ancient Times
This section discusses the history and cultures of Asia during ancient times, covering various regions and civilizations.

Ancient China
Ancient China refers to the early Chinese civilization, known for its dynasties, philosophy, and contributions to culture and technology.

The Steppes
The Steppes are vast grassland regions typically associated with the nomadic peoples who migrated across Asia and Europe.

Korea
Korea is a region in East Asia known for its rich history and interactions with neighboring civilizations, including China and Japan.

Japan
Japan is an island nation in East Asia, noted for its historical isolation and unique cultural developments.

Southeast Asia
Southeast Asia is a diverse region with a complex history involving trade, colonization, and cultural exchanges among various groups.

Vedic India
Vedic India refers to the culture and society in the Indian subcontinent during the Vedic period, marked by the composition of the Vedas and early Hindu development.

Maurya Empire
The Maurya Empire was a vast and influential ancient Indian empire, known for its political unification and cultural achievements under rulers like Ashoka.

Mediterranean Peoples
This section addresses the various peoples and cultures that thrived around the Mediterranean Sea in ancient history.

Ancient Greece
Ancient Greece is known as the cradle of Western civilization, contributing significantly to art, philosophy, and politics.

Hellenistic Era
The Hellenistic Era marks the period following the conquests of Alexander the Great, characterized by the spread of Greek culture across the Mediterranean and Near East.

Roman Republic
The Roman Republic was a period of ancient Roman civilization characterized by a complex system of governance and significant expansion of territory.

Age of Augustus
The Age of Augustus refers to the period of Roman history under the first emperor, marked by peace, stability, and cultural flourishing.

Roman Empire
The Roman Empire was one of the most powerful entities in the ancient world, known for its extensive territorial conquests, governance, and cultural achievements.

The Americas in Ancient Times
This section covers the early cultures, civilizations, and significant events in the Americas before European contact.

Populating the Americas
This refers to the migration and settlement of peoples in the American continents, shaping the diverse cultures that emerged.

Bantu Migrations
The Bantu migrations involved the movement of Bantu-speaking peoples across Africa, leading to significant cultural and linguistic changes.

Kingdom of Kush
The Kingdom of Kush was an ancient civilization located to the south of Egypt, known for its rich resources and interactions with its neighbor.

North Africas Mediterranean Connections
This concept explores the historical trade and cultural exchanges between North African societies and Mediterranean peoples.

Age of Religion, 500–1200 CE
A historical period characterized by significant religious movements and developments, particularly the rise of Islam and various empires of faith.

Empires of Faith
Chapter 10 focuses on the Empires of Faith, detailing their impacts and interactions within the historical context of the period.

data.entity_name: The Rise of Islam and the Caliphates
data.content:
The Rise of Islam and the Caliphates
Chapter 11 addresses the emergence of Islam and the establishment of the Caliphates, exploring their influence on society and politics.

data.entity_name: India, the Indian Ocean Basin, and East Asia
data.content:
India, the Indian Ocean Basin, and East Asia
Chapter 12 examines trade, cultural exchanges, and interactions across regions including India, the Indian Ocean, and East Asia during this era.

data.entity_name: The Post-Roman West and the Crusading Movement
data.content:
The Post-Roman West and the Crusading Movement
Chapter 13 discusses the socio-political landscape following the fall of the Roman Empire, with focus on the Crusading Movement and its implications.

Pax Mongolica
Pax Mongolica refers to the period of peace and stability established by the Mongol Empire, facilitating trade and cultural exchange across Asia during the 13th and 14th centuries.

data.entity_name: The Steppe Empire of the Mongols
data.content:
The Steppe Empire of the Mongols
The Steppe Empire of the Mongols was a vast empire that emerged under the leadership of Chinggis Khan, significantly impacting trade, culture, and political dynamics in the region.

Chinggis Khan
Chinggis Khan was the founder of the Mongol Empire, uniting the Mongol tribes and initiating campaigns that expanded the empire across much of Asia during the early 13th century.

Song China
Song China refers to the period in Chinese history (960–1279) known for its cultural achievements, economic prosperity, and advancements in technology and governance.

Sub-Saharan Africa
Sub-Saharan Africa refers to the region of the African continent lying south of the Sahara Desert, home to diverse cultures, societies, and historical developments.

The Black Death
The Black Death was a devastating global epidemic of bubonic plague that swept through Europe and Asia in the 14th century, leading to significant social and economic upheaval.

data.entity_name: Climate Change in the Fourteenth Century
data.content:
Climate Change in the Fourteenth Century
The climate change during the 14th century contributed to widespread famine and migration, significantly impacting populations across Asia and Europe.

Ottomans, Mamluks, and Ming
The Ottoman, Mamluk, and Ming empires represent significant political powers in the historical landscape of the 14th to 17th centuries, each with its unique influence and interactions.

Appendix A Glossary
Appendix A provides a glossary of key terms used throughout the textbook, enhancing comprehension of historical concepts and terminology.

Map and Timelines
Appendix B includes maps and timelines that illustrate the geographical and chronological contexts of historical events covered in the textbook.

Recommended Resources for the Study of World History
Appendix D offers a list of resources for further exploration of world history topics and themes, aimed at enhancing academic research.
